facts.statement: Fire apparatus access roads shall extend to within 45 m of all portions of the facility and all portions of the exterior walls of the first story of the building, measured by an approved route around the exterior.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 503.1.1 — fire apparatus access road maximum reach
exceptions: Fire official may increase 45 m where building is fully sprinklered per Section 903.3.1.1, 903.3.1.2 or 903.3.1.3
Fire official may increase where access roads cannot be installed due to topography, waterways, nonnegotiable grades or similar
Fire official may increase where there are not more than two Group R-3 or Group U occupancies
Fire official may exempt or modify for solar photovoltaic power generation facilities
facts.source_quote: Approved fire apparatus access roads shall be provided for every facility, building or portion of a building hereafter constructed or moved into or within the jurisdiction. The fire apparatus access road shall comply with the requirements of this section and shall extend to within 45 m of all portions of the facility and all portions of the exterior walls of the first story of the building as measured by an approved route around the exterior of the building or facility.

facts.statement: Fire apparatus access roads shall be designed and maintained to support the imposed loads of fire apparatus and shall be surfaced to provide all-weather driving capabilities.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 503.2.3 — fire apparatus access road surface
facts.source_quote: Fire apparatus access roads shall be designed and maintained to support the imposed loads of fire apparatus and shall be surfaced so as to provide all-weather driving capabilities.

facts.statement: When a lock is changed or rekeyed, the building operator shall immediately notify the Fire official and provide the new key, and the new key shall be secured in the key box.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 506.2 — key box maintenance
facts.source_quote: The operator of the building shall immediately notify the Fire official and provide the new key where a lock is changed or rekeyed. The key to such lock shall be secured in the key box.

facts.statement: Where a portion of the facility or building is more than 120 m from a hydrant on a fire apparatus access road (measured by an approved route around the exterior), on-site fire hydrants and mains shall be provided where required by the Fire official.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 507.5.1 — on-site hydrant trigger distance
exceptions: Group R-3 and Group U occupancies — distance requirement is 180 m (Exception 1)
Buildings fully sprinklered per Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2 — distance requirement is 180 m (Exception 2)
facts.source_quote: Where a portion of the facility or building hereafter constructed or moved into or within the jurisdiction is more than 120 m from a hydrant on a fire apparatus access road, as measured by an approved route around the exterior of the facility or building, on-site fire hydrants and mains shall be provided where required by the Fire official.

facts.statement: For Group R-3 and Group U occupancies, the on-site hydrant distance requirement shall be 180 m.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 507.5.1 Exception 1 — R-3/U hydrant distance
facts.source_quote: For Group R-3 and Group U occupancies, the distance requirement shall be 180 m.

facts.statement: For buildings fully sprinklered per Section 903.3.1.1 or 903.3.1.2, the on-site hydrant distance requirement shall be 180 m.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 507.5.1 Exception 2 — sprinklered hydrant distance
facts.source_quote: For buildings equipped throughout with an approved automatic sprinkler system installed in accordance with Section 903.3.1.1or 903.3.1.2, the distance requirement shall be 180 m.

facts.statement: Appendix Table B105.1 fire flow calculations are based on a 138 kPa residual pressure.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Appendix B105.1 — fire flow residual pressure basis
facts.source_quote: Appendix Table B105.1 bases fire flow on the type of construction and the square meter of the fire flow calculation area. All calculations in the table are based on a 138 kPa residual pressure.

facts.statement: Acceptable in-building two-way emergency responder communication coverage requires signal strength measurements meeting requirements in 95 percent of all areas and 99 percent of areas designated as critical areas by the Fire official on each floor of the building.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.1 — coverage area threshold (general areas)
facts.source_quote: The building shall be considered to have acceptable in-building, two-way emergency responder communication system coverage where signal strength measurements in 95 percent of all areas and 99 percent of areas designated as critical areas by the Fire official on each floor of the building meet the signal strength requirements in Sections 510.4.1.1 through 510.4.1.3.

facts.statement: Critical areas designated by the Fire official require signal strength compliance in 99 percent of those areas on each floor of the building.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.1 — critical area coverage threshold
facts.source_quote: signal strength measurements in 95 percent of all areas and 99 percent of areas designated as critical areas by the Fire official on each floor of the building meet the signal strength requirements in Sections 510.4.1.1 through 510.4.1.3

facts.statement: The inbound signal level shall be a minimum of -95 dBm throughout the coverage area and sufficient to provide not less than a Delivered Audio Quality (DAQ) of 3.0 or an equivalent SINR for the technology.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.1.1 — minimum inbound signal strength
facts.source_quote: The inbound signal level shall be a minimun of -95dBm throughout the coverage area and sufficient to provide not less than a Delivered Audio Quality (DAQ) of 3.0 or an equivalent Signal-to-Interference-Plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) applicable to the technology for either analog or digital signals.

facts.statement: Voice communications shall provide not less than a Delivered Audio Quality (DAQ) of 3.0 throughout the coverage area.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.1.1 — minimum delivered audio quality
facts.source_quote: sufficient to provide not less than a Delivered Audio Quality (DAQ) of 3.0

facts.statement: Where a donor antenna exists, isolation shall be maintained between the donor antenna and all inside antennas to not less than 20 dB greater than the system gain under all operating conditions.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.4 Item 4 — donor antenna isolation margin
facts.source_quote: Where a donor antenna exists, isolation shall be maintained between the donor antenna and all inside antennas to not less than 20dB greater than the system gain under all operating conditions.

facts.statement: All signal booster components shall be contained in a NEMA 4-type waterproof cabinet.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.4 Item 1 — signal booster cabinet rating
facts.source_quote: All signal booster components shall be contained in a National Electrical Manufacturer's Association (NEMA) 4-type waterproof cabinet.

facts.statement: Battery systems used for the emergency power source shall be contained in a NEMA 3R or higher-rated cabinet.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.4 Item 2 — battery cabinet rating
facts.source_quote: Battery systems used for the emergency power source shall be contained in a NEMA 3R or higher-rated cabinet.

facts.statement: An automatic supervisory signal shall be generated for low-battery capacity at 70 percent reduction of operating capacity.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.5 Item 5 — low battery supervisory threshold
facts.source_quote: Low-battery capacity at 70-percent reduction of operating capacity.

facts.statement: The in-building two-way emergency responder communication coverage system shall be monitored by a listed fire alarm control unit, or where approved by the Fire official, shall sound an audible signal at a constantly attended on-site location, with automatic supervisory signals for eight specified failure modes.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.5 — required automatic supervisory signals
facts.source_quote: The in-building, two-way emergency responder communication coverage system shall be monitored by a listed fire alarm control unit, or where approved by the Fire official, shall sound an audible signal at a constantly attended on-site location.

facts.statement: Class III standpipe systems shall be installed where the floor level of the highest story is located more than 9 m above the lowest level of the fire department vehicle access.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 905.3.1 Item 2 — highest story above access threshold
facts.source_quote: The floor level of the highest story is located more than 9 m above the lowest level of the fire department vehicle access.

facts.statement: Class III standpipe systems shall be installed throughout buildings where four or more stories are above or below grade plane.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 905.3.1 Item 1 — story count threshold
exceptions: Standpipe systems are not required in Group R-3 occupancies (Section 905.3 Exception)
facts.source_quote: Four or more stories are above or below grade plane.

facts.statement: Portable fire extinguishers shall be installed within 9 m distance of travel from commercial cooking equipment and from domestic cooking equipment in Group I-1; I-2 Condition 1; and R-2 college dormitory occupancies.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 906.1 Item 2 — extinguisher distance from cooking equipment
facts.source_quote: Within 9 m distance of travel from commercial cooking equipment and from domestic cooking equipment in Group I-1; I-2, Condition 1; and R-2 college dormitory occupancies.

facts.statement: In Group R-2 occupancies, where each dwelling unit is provided with a portable fire extinguisher having a minimum rating of 1-A:10-B:C, portable fire extinguishers shall be required only in locations specified in Items 2 through 6.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 906.1 Exception 1 — R-2 per-unit extinguisher rating
facts.source_quote: In Group R-2 occupancies, portable fire extinguishers shall be required only in locations specified in Items 2 through 6 where each dwelling unit is provided with a portable fire extinguisher having a minimum rating of 1-A:10-B: C.

facts.statement: In Group E occupancies, where each classroom is provided with a portable fire extinguisher having a minimum rating of 2-A:20-B:C, portable fire extinguishers shall be required only in locations specified in Items 2 through 6.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 906.1 Exception 2 — Group E classroom extinguisher rating
facts.source_quote: In Group E occupancies, portable fire extinguishers shall be required only in locations specified in Items 2 through 6 where each classroom is provided with a portable fire extinguisher having a minimum rating of 2-A:20-B:C.

facts.statement: Each vehicle in qualifying Group S storage areas shall be equipped with a 4.5 kg, 40A:80B:C extinguisher affixed to the vehicle using an approved mounting bracket.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 906.1 Exception 3.2 — vehicle-mounted extinguisher size
facts.source_quote: Each vehicle shall be equipped with a 4.5 kg, 40A:80B:C extinguisher affixed to the vehicle using a mounting bracket approved by the extinguisher manufacturer or the Fire official for vehicular use.

facts.statement: Not less than two spare extinguishers of equal or greater rating shall be available on-site to replace a discharged extinguisher in Group S storage areas using vehicle-mounted extinguishers.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 906.1 Exception 3.3 — spare extinguisher minimum
facts.source_quote: Not less than two spare extinguishers of equal or greater rating shall be available on-site to replace a discharged extinguisher.

facts.statement: A manual fire alarm system that activates the occupant notification system shall be installed in Group A occupancies where the occupant load due to the assembly occupancy is 300 or more.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 907.2.1 — Group A occupant load alarm trigger
facts.source_quote: A manual fire alarm system that activates the occupant notification system in accordance with Section 907.5 shall be installed in Group A occupancies where the occupant load due to the assembly occupancy is 300 or more, or where the Group A occupant load is more than 100 persons above or below the lowest level of exit discharge.

facts.statement: A manual fire alarm system shall also be installed in Group A occupancies where the Group A occupant load is more than 100 persons above or below the lowest level of exit discharge.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 907.2.1 — Group A occupant load above/below exit discharge
facts.source_quote: where the Group A occupant load is more than 100 persons above or below the lowest level of exit discharge.

facts.statement: Where the fire department connection is not visible to approaching fire apparatus on existing buildings, signs shall have the letters 'FDC' not less than 150 mm high.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 912.2.2 — FDC sign letter height (FDC)
facts.source_quote: Such sign shall have the letters "FDC" not less than 150 mm high and words in letters not less than 50 mm high or an arrow to indicate the location.

facts.statement: Where the fire department connection is not visible to approaching fire apparatus on existing buildings, words on the sign shall be in letters not less than 50 mm high (or an arrow indicating the location).
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 912.2.2 — FDC sign supplemental letter height
facts.source_quote: and words in letters not less than 50 mm high or an arrow to indicate the location.

facts.statement: The fire pump room shall be maintained above 5 degrees C at all times; if the engine requires a higher temperature, the manufacturer's recommendations shall be followed.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 913.3 — fire pump room minimum temperature
facts.source_quote: 913.3 درجة حرارة غرفة المضخات: يُحافظ على حرارة غرفة المضخة فوق 5°C دائماً.

facts.statement: Cables for fire pump circuits may be protected by concrete encasement of not less than 50 mm.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 913.2.2 Item 4 — concrete encasement minimum thickness
facts.source_quote: تغليف الكبل بخرسانة ≥ 50 مم

facts.statement: Underground buildings with floors used for human occupancy that are greater than 9 m below the floor of the level of exit discharge are required to be provided with smoke control per SBC 201 Section 405.5.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 909.1 — underground smoke control trigger depth
facts.source_quote: Underground buildings with floors used for human occupancy that are greater than 9 m below the floor of the level of exit discharge are required to be provided with smoke control (see SBC 201 Section 405.5).

facts.statement: During the 40 kW exposure of NFPA 286, flames shall not spread to the ceiling.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.1.1.1 Item 1 — 40 kW exposure ceiling flame criterion
facts.source_quote: During the 40 kW exposure, flames shall not spread to the ceiling.

facts.statement: During NFPA 286 testing, the peak heat release rate shall not exceed 800 kW.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.1.1.1 Item 4 — peak heat release rate limit
facts.source_quote: The peak heat release rate throughout the test shall not exceed 800 kW.

facts.statement: During NFPA 286 testing, the total smoke released shall not exceed 1,000 m2.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.1.1.1 Item 5 — total smoke release limit
facts.source_quote: The total smoke released throughout the test shall not exceed 1,000 m².

facts.statement: Class A interior wall and ceiling finish materials (per ASTM E84 or UL 723) have a flame spread index in the range 0-25 and a smoke-developed index of 0-450.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.1.2 — Class A flame spread limit
facts.source_quote: Class A: flame spread index 0–25; smoke-developed index 0–450.

facts.statement: Class B interior wall and ceiling finish materials (per ASTM E84 or UL 723) have a flame spread index in the range 26-75 and a smoke-developed index of 0-450.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.1.2 — Class B flame spread upper limit
facts.source_quote: Class B: flame spread index 26–75; smoke-developed index 0–450.

facts.statement: Class C interior wall and ceiling finish materials (per ASTM E84 or UL 723) have a flame spread index in the range 76-200 and a smoke-developed index of 0-450.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.1.2 — Class C flame spread upper limit
facts.source_quote: Class C: flame spread index 76–200; smoke-developed index 0–450.

facts.statement: Interior finish materials regulated by Chapter 8 shall be applied or fastened so they will not readily become detached when subjected to room temperatures of 93 degrees C for not less than 30 minutes.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.2 — interior finish stability temperature
facts.source_quote: Interior finish materials regulated by this chapter shall be applied or otherwise fastened in such a manner that such materials will not readily become detached where subjected to room temperatures of 93°C for not less than 30 minutes.

facts.statement: Interior finish stability shall be maintained for not less than 30 minutes at the test temperature.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.2 — interior finish stability duration
facts.source_quote: for not less than 30 minutes

facts.statement: Section 2808 governs storage and processing of wood chips, hogged material, fines, compost, solid biomass feedstock and raw product associated with yard waste, agro-industrial and recycling facilities.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Chapter 28 Section 2808 — applicability
facts.source_quote: SECTION 2808 STORAGE AND PROCESSING OF WOOD CHIPS, HOGGED MATERIAL, FINES, COMPOST, SOLID BIOMASS FEEDSTOCK AND RAW PRODUCT ASSOCIATED WITH YARD WASTE, AGRO-INDUSTRIAL AND RECYCLING FACILITIES

facts.statement: Commercial cooking systems regulated by Section 904.13 require automatic fire extinguishing systems compliant with this section in addition to portable extinguishers.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 904.13 — commercial cooking system suppression scope
facts.source_quote: Commercial cooking systems shall be provided with an automatic fire-extinguishing system.

facts.statement: Standpipe systems are allowed to be combined with automatic sprinkler systems.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 905.3 — combined standpipe/sprinkler permission
exceptions: Standpipe systems are not required in Group R-3 occupancies
facts.source_quote: Standpipe systems shall be installed where required by Sections 905.3.1 through 905.3.8. Standpipe systems are allowed to be combined with automatic sprinkler systems.

facts.statement: Fire pumps shall be inspected, tested and maintained in accordance with NFPA 25.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 913.5 — fire pump testing standard
facts.source_quote: 913.5 الاختبار والصيانة (Testing & Maintenance): المضخات تُفحص وتُختبر وتُصان وفق NFPA 25.

facts.statement: Suction, discharge and bypass valves for the fire pump shall be supervised in the open position by one of four approved methods (central-station signaling; local supervised signal; locking valves open; sealing valves with weekly inspections).
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 913.4 — valve supervision methods count
facts.source_quote: 913.4 مراقبة الصمامات (Valve Supervision): صمامات السحب والطرد والتجاوز لمضخة الحريق تُراقب في وضع "مفتوح" بإحدى طرق

facts.statement: High-rise facilities require smokeproof exit enclosures in accordance with Sections 909.20 and 1023.11 (cross-referenced from SBC 201 Section 403.5.4).
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 909.20 — high-rise smokeproof exit enclosures requirement
facts.source_quote: High-rise facilities require smokeproof exit enclosures in accordance with Sections 909.20 and 1023.11 (see SBC 201 Section 403.5.4).

facts.statement: Portable fire extinguishers shall be installed on each floor of structures under construction, except Group R-3 occupancies, in accordance with Section 3316.1.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 906.1 Item 4 — construction-site extinguishers
facts.source_quote: On each floor of structures under construction, except Group R-3 occupancies, in accordance with Section 3316.1.

facts.statement: The fire-barrier opening limits do not apply where adjoining floor areas are equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system per Section 903.3.1.1.
facts.scope: SBC-201 Section 707.6 Exception 1 — sprinkler exemption
facts.source_quote: Adjoining floor areas equipped throughout with an automatic sprinkler system per Section 903.3.1.1 (Exception 1)

facts.statement: Fire command centers are required where mandated by other code sections, in all buildings classified as high-rise buildings by SBC 201, and in F-1 and S-1 occupancies with a building footprint exceeding the threshold specified in SBC 201.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 508.1 — fire command center applicability
facts.source_quote: Where required by other sections of this code and in all buildings classified as high-rise buildings by SBC 201 and in all F-1 and S-1 occupancies with a building footprint greater than

facts.statement: Active RF-emitting devices used for in-building two-way emergency responder communication coverage systems shall have built-in oscillation detection and control circuitry.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.4 Item 5 — oscillation detection requirement
facts.source_quote: Active RF-emitting devices used for in-building, twoway emergency responder communication coverage systems shall have built-in oscillation detection and control circuitry.

facts.statement: Equipment shall have FCC or other radio licensing authority certification and be suitable for public safety use prior to installation.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.4 Item 3 — radio licensing certification
facts.source_quote: Equipment shall have FCC or other radio licensing authority certification and be suitable for public safety use prior to installation.

facts.statement: Automatic supervisory signals shall include loss of normal AC power supply.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.5 Item 1 — AC power loss monitoring
facts.source_quote: 1. Loss of normal AC power supply.

facts.statement: Automatic supervisory signals shall include failure of active RF-emitting devices.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.5 Item 4 — RF device failure monitoring
facts.source_quote: 4. Failure of active RF-emitting device(s).

facts.statement: Automatic supervisory signals shall include malfunction of the donor antenna.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.5 Item 3 — donor antenna supervisory
facts.source_quote: 3. Malfunction of the donor antenna(s).

facts.statement: Automatic supervisory signals shall include oscillation of active RF-emitting devices.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.5 Item 8 — oscillation supervisory
facts.source_quote: 8. Oscillation of active RF-emitting device(s).

facts.statement: Automatic supervisory signals shall include system battery charger failure.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.5 Item 2 — battery charger failure
facts.source_quote: 2. System battery charger(s) failure.

facts.statement: Automatic supervisory signals shall include failure of critical system components.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.5 Item 6 — critical component failure
facts.source_quote: 6. Failure of critical system components.

facts.statement: Automatic supervisory signals shall include the communications link between the fire alarm system and the in-building two-way emergency responder communication coverage system.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.5 Item 7 — comms link supervisory
facts.source_quote: 7. The communications link between the fire alarm system and the in-building, two-way emergency responder communication coverage system.

facts.statement: Installation of amplification systems or systems that operate on or provide the means to cause interference on any in-building two-way emergency responder communication coverage network shall be coordinated and approved by the Fire official.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 510.4.2.4 Item 6 — Fire official coordination
facts.source_quote: The installation of amplification systems or systems that operate on or provide the means to cause interference on any in-building, two-way emergency respondercommunication coverage network shall be coordinated and approved by the Fire official.

facts.statement: Standpipe systems are not required in Group R-3 occupancies.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 905.3 Exception — R-3 standpipe exemption
facts.source_quote: Exception: Standpipe systems are not required in Group R-3 occupancies.

facts.statement: Textile wall coverings used as interior wall finish materials, including woven, nonwoven, napped, tufted, looped or similar surfaces, shall be tested in the manner intended for use using the product mounting system, including adhesive, and shall comply with Section 803.1.1, 803.5.1 or 803.5.2.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.5 — textile wall covering test requirement
facts.source_quote: Where used as interior wall finish materials, textile wall coverings, including materials having a woven, nonwoven, napped, tufted, looped or similar surface, shall be tested in the manner intended for use, using the product mounting system, including adhesive, and shall comply with the requirements of Section 803.1.1, 803.5.1 or 803.5.2.

facts.statement: Fire-retardant coatings used to achieve required flame spread or smoke-developed index in existing buildings shall comply with NFPA 703, and the required fire-retardant properties shall be maintained or renewed per the manufacturer's instructions.
facts.scope: SBC-801 Section 803.4 — fire-retardant coating standard
facts.source_quote: The required flame spread or smoke-developed index of surfaces in existing buildings shall be allowed to be achieved by application of approved fire-retardant coatings, paints or solutions to surfaces having a flame spread index exceeding that allowed. Such applications shall comply with NFPA 703 and the required fire retardant properties shall be maintained or renewed in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.
